correctness.rationale: The vertices are all nonempty proper subsets of [n], edges denote disjointness; degree 2^(n-|S|)-1 identifies singleton vertices. Singleton nonadjacency reconstructs every S, hence Aut(B_n)=S_n. Pointwise stabilizers of k chosen subsets act on [n] by coordinate permutations preserving each k-bit signature, so they are trivial exactly when the n signatures are pairwise distinct. The pigeonhole lower bound k>=ceil(log2 n) is attained because n>2^(k-1), so choosing n distinct k-bit words creates nonconstant and pairwise distinct subset rows. Injective word assignments number (2^k)!/(2^k-n)!, each unordered minimum family has k! row orderings. Thus exact count (2^k)!/((2^k-n)! k!); for n=5 k=3 gives 1120 and no pair determines. Independently reviewed finite exhaustive checker for 2<=n<=7 (counts 2,12,12,1120,3360,6720); no finite test substituted for the combinatorial arbitrary-n proof.
